title: Observed flooding, October 2023
summary: New surface water seen by satellite radar after the 2023 Akosombo and Kpong dam spillage.

temporal.note: Union of two radar passes: track 147 on 16 October and track 74 on 23 October 2023

method: Sentinel-1 VV change detection adapted from UN-SPIDER: flood-date backscatter against a 5-scene pre-event median per track (ratio above 1.25 and below -15 dB), slope of 5 degrees or less from the DEM, at least 8 connected pixels. Permanent water removed with JRC Global Surface Water; new water where water occurs at least 10% of the time is classed as ambiguous.
limitations: Shows water on two pass dates only: not peak extent, not a hazard model and not a return-period map.
Radar misses flooding under dense vegetation and among buildings, so both figures are likely under-estimates.
Ambiguous water includes lagoons and salt pans near Ada that flood every year; report the extent as a range of about 38 to 78 square kilometres.
Not yet validated against reported affected communities.

classes.label: Ambiguous seasonal water
classes.description: New water where water has occurred before, so it cannot be put down to the spillage
